## Summary

I implemented digits-only telephone storage with normalization applied before the uniqueness check.

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Relaxed the `telephone` validation pattern from `^[0-9]*$` to `^[-0-9 ()]*$` so punctuated input like `(613) 555-0100` passes `@Valid` on the request DTO (the DTO is regenerated from this spec at build time). Updated the description to document the strip-on-input behavior.

2. **`Telephones.java`** (new) — Small shared helper `digitsOnly(...)` that strips everything but digits, keeping the normalization rule in one place.

3. **`BuildOwner.java`** (POST) — Strips the mapped telephone to digits before publishing the `Owner`, so the stored value — and thus the `telephone` field returned by GET — is digits only. This runs *before* the `ensureUnique` step in the pipeline.

4. **`ApplyOwner.java`** (PUT) — Same digits-only stripping when updating an owner, keeping storage consistent.

5. **`EnsureOwnerUnique.java`** — Telephone comparisons now use `normalizeTelephone(...)` (digit-stripping) on both the candidate and each existing owner, so `(613) 555-0100` and `6135550100` collide as duplicates even if any stored value were ever punctuated.

Both new Cp11 tests pass: `coreStoresDigitsOnly` (formatted input stored/returned as digits) and `functionalityNormalisedDuplicateRejected` (punctuated duplicate → 409), and no existing tests regressed.
